newsitem.title: UK: UK to create regional development agencies by 1999.
newsitem.headline: UK to create regional development agencies by 1999.

text.p: The new Labour government said on Wednesday it would bring forward a bill to establish regional development agencies in England, outside London, as part of its election commitment to decentralise power.
It said that the new agencies would come into operation on April 1, 1999, and that their budgets would be built up by redeploying existing resources.
The functions given to the agencies would include promoting inward investment, helping small businesses and coordinating regional economic development.

They would be expected to work in close cooperation with the government's regional administrative offices, existing non-statutory Regional Chambers established by local authorities, Training and Enterprise Councils and other bodies that promote regional economic development.
